clue.text: Like registered member of club, say, concerned about transport

parts.note: a club is one suit of playing cards, so an example of a card
a business concerned with transport is in the carrying trade

explanation.surface: Describing a club member whose membership is all about getting around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is only a link. The surface suggests a sports or social club, but a club here is a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: A paid-up, officially enrolled party or union member is said to carry a membership card, hence the adjective.

clue.text: Company Law restricting member's deal

indicators.note: restricting means the company and law pieces enclose the member

parts.note: an act is a law passed by Parliament
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Corporate law limiting what a Member of Parliament can agree.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact is a formal agreement or pact between parties.

clue.text: Down under, sport is dominant

definitions.meaning: in Australia the game of Australian football is called Aussie ... or simply ...
to rule is to hold sway or prevail

explanation.surface: In Australia, sport reigns supreme.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian rules football is the national winter sport there, and to rule means to be in control.

clue.text: Thrash in convincing way to show relationship between two sides

indicators.note: in means the word for thrash is placed inside the word for convincing

parts.note: a cogent argument is convincing
to tan someone's hide is to thrash them

explanation.surface: Winning convincingly to show how the two teams compare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' and 'to show' are link words. 'Thrash' looks like a heavy win between two sides.
explanation.definitionFit: In trigonometry the cotangent of an angle is the ratio of the adjacent side to the opposite side.

clue.text: Right time to get up, though unusual

indicators.note: to get up in a down clue means the word for time is read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: The proper hour for rising, even if it seldom happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare means seldom found or uncommon.

clue.text: Poor granny that is suffering an ache

indicators.note: poor signals that the letters are in a bad state and must be rearranged

parts.note: ie is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is

explanation.surface: An unfortunate grandmother in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' is a link. 'Poor' rearranges GRANNY plus IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearning is a longing, an emotional pang for something.

clue.text: Spoiled Roman girl

indicators.note: spoiled signals that the letters of the following word are messed up

explanation.surface: A pampered girl from ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoiled' looks like pampered, but it shuffles ROMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a female first name, as in Bellini's opera heroine.

clue.text: Beat up and beat again — with a spoon, perhaps?

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for beat is read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: to flog is to beat
to club is to beat, here the second beating

explanation.surface: A thug beats someone, then beats them again with a kitchen spoon.
explanation.walkthrough: A spoon was an old name for a lofted wooden club, roughly a modern 3-wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The spoon was a traditional wooden club used in the game on the links.

clue.text: Unemotional team-leader in firm

indicators.note: in means that letter goes inside the word for firm

parts.note: firm and solid both mean hard and stable

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of the word team is used

explanation.surface: A captain in a business who shows no feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid means impassive, showing little emotion.

clue.text: Armed unit holding back gunners obtaining medals, perhaps

indicators.note: holding means the armed unit's letters wrap around another piece

parts.note: a militia is an armed body of citizen soldiers

indicators.note: back means the word for gunners is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: A military unit that keeps the artillery in reserve and wins decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Armed unit' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the outer piece, and the definition sits at the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: Militaria are collectable military objects, of which medals are a typical example.

clue.text: Son tucked into grub in temporary accommodation

indicators.note: tucked into means the letter for son is placed inside the other word

parts.note: to grub is to dig or rummage, as does to root

explanation.surface: A boy eating his food while staying somewhere for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like food for 'tucked into', but here it is the verb to root about.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a perch where birds rest, and colloquially any place to stay for the night.

clue.text: Not appearing to have an ability to absorb science initially

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A

indicators.note: to absorb means the word for ability takes another letter inside it

parts.note: a bent is a natural talent or aptitude

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the word science is used

explanation.surface: Someone who seems unable to take in any science.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives S, which 'to absorb' puts inside BENT; A in front makes ABSENT. The filed ASSENT is one letter off and unparsed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent is not present, so is failing to show up.

clue.text: Peacemakers left dreadful criminal

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces
dreadful and awful are synonyms

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers leave behind a terrible offender.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe acts that break the law, so they are synonyms as adjectives.

clue.text: One who prevents front coming off hat

indicators.note: front coming off means the opening letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a stopper is one who stops, that is prevents, something

explanation.surface: A guard keeping someone's front from falling off their hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first letter, S, of STOPPER leaves the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A top hat is often called a topper informally.

clue.text: Someone's picture -seaside artist takes it

parts.note: a port is a seaside town or harbour
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter by the sea gets a picture of somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painting or photograph of a particular person.

clue.text: Made unauthorised collection and put a bit on a horse

definitions.meaning: to snaffle is informally to take something without permission

definitions.text: put a bit on a horse
definitions.meaning: a snaffle is a simple jointed bit for a horse's mouth, so to snaffle a horse is to fit one

explanation.surface: A horse thief takes the animal and puts a bit in its mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Snaffling means pinching something, and also bridling a horse with that particular bit.

clue.text: Nationalist seen to lose resolution — doubly so

parts.note: to flag is to tire and lose determination
to waver is to falter and become undecided

explanation.surface: A patriot who seems to lose nerve twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly so' says the phrase 'lose resolution' is used twice, once for each half.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag-waver is an ardent patriot who loudly shows national pride.

clue.text: Flower or plant seen around north before fall

indicators.note: around means the word for plant goes round the letter for north

parts.note: to plant seeds is to sow
a drop is a fall

explanation.surface: A gardener choosing between a flower and some plant before autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen' and 'before' are links; 'fall' looks like autumn but means DROP.
explanation.definitionFit: The snowdrop is a small white flower blooming in late winter.

clue.text: Massage back wound — result of explosion

indicators.note: back means the word for massage is read in reverse

parts.note: to massage is to rub
to sting is to hurt or wound

explanation.surface: A masseur treats a back injury caused by a blast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like part of the body being massaged, but it turns RUB into BUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Bursting is the breaking apart caused when something blows up.

clue.text: Take chance with fish shop

parts.note: to bet is to gamble, to take a chance
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Gambling on a fish shop.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for informing on them, so to betray them.

clue.text: Scholar meeting master primarily to express disapproval of cane

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, stands for a graduate scholar

indicators.note: primarily means just the opening letter of the word master is used

parts.note: to boo is to jeer in disapproval

explanation.surface: A student and teacher jeering at a schoolroom cane.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamboo is a woody grass whose hollow stems are used as canes.

clue.text: Completed fitting, and not before time

parts.note: something over is finished or completed
due means proper or fitting

explanation.surface: A fitting finished, but only at the last moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdue means late, arriving after it should have.

clue.text: Reject blue act to open with

indicators.note: to open with means the word for act comes first, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act on stage
blue and down both mean sad

explanation.surface: Refusing a risqué stage act as a show opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' suggests smutty material, but here it means sad, DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn down an offer is to refuse it.

clue.text: Concentrated English studies put over

indicators.note: put over in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: dens are studies, private rooms for work

explanation.surface: Intensive English study placed above other subjects.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense means thick or compact, closely packed together.

clue.text: Smart belt he put on cloak

indicators.note: put on means the second piece is attached after the first

parts.note: a smart belt is a sharp blow, a swat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stylish belt worn by a man over his cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like stylish dress, but a smart belt here is a stinging blow.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap or envelop, as one might cloak something.

clue.text: One taking part in revolution in European city

indicators.note: taking part in means the numeral one goes inside the word for revolution

parts.note: a turn is one revolution
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone joining an uprising in a Continental city.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in northern Italy.

clue.text: Long established in bachelorhood

indicators.note: established in means the answer sits inside the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A long-standing single life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective for the bachelorhood, but it is the verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to long or yearn for it.

clue.text: It can be a crime to smuggle in a foreigner

indicators.note: to smuggle in means the second a is slipped inside the word for crime

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing or offence

explanation.surface: Smuggling an illegal immigrant can be a criminal offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It can be' is a link. The second A goes inside SIN to give SIAN, after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: An Asian is a person from Asia, so a foreigner from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Got back from hide in the long grass

indicators.note: in means the word for hide is placed inside the grass

parts.note: reeds are tall grasses growing by water
to hide something is to cover it

explanation.surface: Retrieving something from a hiding place in tall grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover is to regain or retrieve what was lost.

clue.text: Coming back to harvest fruit given a half-chance

parts.note: to harvest is to reap
a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: half here means only the latter three letters of the word chance are kept

explanation.surface: Returning to gather fruit after being given only a slim opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps NCE, the back half of CHANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reappearance is a return or showing up again.
